name: CFPB complaints × OT
label: CFPB complaints × OT: killed at burn-in (negative result)
learning_link_text: CFPB complaints: what the forecast was going to test (learning page)
card_desc_html:
Burn-in median next-month W₂² 0.0064 < half-sample noise floor 0.0269: month-to-month change in the
        cross-company shape of complaints is below sampling noise, so the pre-registered rule killed the object.
        No out-of-sample run.
verdict_html: The burn-in median next-month W₂² was 0.0064, below the half-sample noise floor of 0.0269 (ratio 0.237). By the pre-registered rule the object is killed: from one month to the next, the shape of complaints across companies moved less than two random halves of the same month differ. A forecast of that month-to-month change could not be told apart from sampling noise, so nothing was scored and no replacement object is proposed.
what_html: Each month, the spread of complaint counts across companies in the CFPB consumer-complaint file: the equal-weighted distribution of log(1 + complaints) among companies with at least one complaint that month, with three pinned credit-bureau names left out. Two optimal-transport methods were pre-registered against simple baselines: an equal-weight W₂ barycenter of the baselines (the average of their quantile functions) and a Wasserstein autoregression of the monthly quantile functions. The plain-language explanation is on the learning page.
rule_html: The half-sample distance is the noise floor: split each month's companies at random into two halves and measure how far apart their quantile functions are. If consecutive months are closer than that, the month-to-month signal is below the noise and there is nothing for a forecast to beat.
record_note_html: The design JSON keeps oos_authorized: false, and that flag is not the switch. Because the burn-in kill fired, an out-of-sample run of this object would not start even if an approval file were written later. A different object would need its own pre-registration.
